column2: On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), who said: I was behind the Prophet ﷺ one day, and he said to me: “O young man,
I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah.

Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has already written for you; and if they were to gather together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something Allah has already written against you.

The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: “A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.” In a narration other than al-Tirmidhī's: “Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you. Get to know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in times of hardship.

Know that what has missed you was not going to befall you, and what has befallen you was not going to miss you. Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease.”

His words, “Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you”, mean: guard the limits set by Allah by carrying out His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, believing the reports [of revelation] and worshipping Him in accordance with what He has prescribed,

not according to whims and innovations, and Allah will protect you in the matters of your religion and your worldly life, as a fitting recompense; that is, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: the deed is guarding, and the recompense is guarding.

His words, “Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you (tujāhaka)”: tujāhaka means in front of you, as in the other narration, “Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you (amāmaka)”. The meaning is: you will find Him surrounding you with His care and looking after you in the matters of your religion and your worldly life.
His words, “When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah”, correspond to the saying of the Exalted, “You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help” [al-Fātiḥah 1:5],

for asking Allah is supplication, and supplication is worship. The meaning is that the Muslim worships Allah alone, asks Him to fulfil his needs and seeks His help in all his affairs, worldly and otherworldly,
while taking the lawful means and asking Allah to make the means beneficial, as he ﷺ said: “Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up.” Reported by Muslim (2664).

His words, “Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you…” up to his words, “The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried”: having said that one asks Allah alone and seeks help from Allah alone, he told us that everything is in His hand,

that none can withhold what He gives and none can give what He withholds, that nothing falls outside His will and wish, and that people cannot benefit a person with anything Allah has not decreed, nor harm him with anything Allah has not decreed;

and that everything that happens or does not happen has already been settled by the divine decision and decree. That is why he said, “The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried”, meaning that everything that will be has been settled and written and must inevitably happen.

The lifting of the pens and the drying of the pages means that everything decreed has been finished with, by being written in the Preserved Tablet, so it must happen as it was decreed. These sentences affirm belief in the decree, which is one of the six foundations of faith set out in the well-known hadith of Jibrīl.

His words, “Get to know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in times of hardship”, mean that whoever devotes his deeds sincerely to Allah in times of ease and plenty will find good from Allah, and harm warded off from him, in times of hardship and distress, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

“And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect” [al-Ṭalāq 65:2–3]; and He said: “Had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected” [al-Ṣāffāt 37:143–144]; and as in the story of the three who took shelter for the night in a cave,

when a rock rolled down and blocked the mouth of the cave. They sought nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through righteous deeds they had done in times of ease: one of them sought it through his dutifulness to his parents, the second through his keeping a trust, growing it and returning it to its owner,

and the third through his leaving an indecency for the sake of Allah after he had been able to commit it. Allah removed their distress and took away the harm that had befallen them, and the rock moved until they were able to get out of the cave. Reported by al-Bukhārī (5974) and Muslim (2743).

His words, “Know that what has missed you was not going to befall you, and what has befallen you was not going to miss you”, mean that what Allah has decreed you will be safe from will not happen to you, and what He has decreed will happen to you must inevitably happen,

because what Allah wills happens and what He does not will does not happen. Everything Allah has decreed to happen must come into being and will not fail to, and there is no way for you to obtain or reach anything that has not been decreed for you.
His words, “Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease”: these three sentences show that victory comes with patience, relief with distress,

and ease with hardship; that patience results in victory by the permission of Allah; that Allah removes distress and hardship with the relief that follows them; and that hardship is followed by ease from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Allah protects whoever guards His limits, in his religion and his worldly life.
Whoever neglects the limits set by Allah does not receive protection from Allah, as He said: “They forgot Allah, so He forgot them” [al-Tawbah 9:67].
The recompense is of the same kind as the deed: the deed is guarding, and the recompense is guarding.
The servant devotes his worship and his seeking of help to his Lord alone.
The hadith affirms belief in the decree.
People can neither benefit nor harm except when the benefit or harm has been decreed by Allah.
No benefit comes to anyone unless it has been decreed, and no harm is warded off from him unless that has been decreed: what Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen.
Patience is followed by victory.
Distress is followed by relief.
Hardship is followed by ease.
The Prophet ﷺ was humble and gentle with the young.
It is good to preface an important matter with something that makes people eager to hear it,
since he said: “Shall I not teach you some words?”
